newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down awaiting Finance One.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down awaiting Finance One.

text.p: Thai stocks closed lower on Thursday ahead of a resumption of trade in shares of troubled finance firm Finance One Plc which is widely expected to drag the market down on Friday, traders said.
The SET Index ended down 4.66 points or 0.83 percent at 558.17. The SET 50 closed down 0.39 points or 0.96 percent to 40.30. Turnover was 2.60 billion baht.

"Everyone, including the foreigners, are waiting for the resumption in trade of Finance One tomorrow," said Tanadech Mahapokai, first assistant vice president at The Book Club Finance and Securities Plc.

The market showed little reaction to central bank data released earlier, which provided few surprises and served primarily to confirm figures already released by government officials or agencies earlier this month, traders said.

With Finance One's resumption expected to see the market fall on Friday, investors were moving out of finance stocks on Thursday and selling short in the hope of buying holdings back more cheaply, traders said.
"People were shorting large capitalised stocks today and are hoping to buy them back more cheaply tomorrow," Tanadech said.

Shares of Finance One, formerly the country's leading finance firm, last traded in February at 23.75 baht. The shares have been suspended for three months pending now-aborted merger plans aimed at improving the ailing firm's financial stability.
The shares are widely tipped by analysts to be heavily traded on Friday at between four and seven baht, adversely affecting the finance sector stocks and the overall market.

Finance stocks discounted 2.58 percent today as the sector braced itself. Dhana Siam Plc lost two baht to 18.25, while National Finance and Securities Plc dipped 1.50 to 19.00 and Bangkok Bank Plc was unchanged at 146.
